summary.headline: Trustees approved two staff promotions, authorized all board members to sign payables, and discussed building and IT maintenance.
summary.summary: The Southborough Library Board of Trustees unanimously approved the promotion of two staff members to part-time library associate positions. The board voted to authorize all trustees to sign off on payable batches and reviewed end-of-fiscal-year budget balances. Trustees also discussed an upcoming staff training on dementia, ongoing facilities and landscaping maintenance, and long-term planning for roughly $30,000 in IT infrastructure rewiring.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board approved the meeting minutes from June 8 as written and handled procedural logistics regarding member signatures for warrant authorizations.
key_details: Approved June 8 meeting minutes.
Noted that members must physically visit the library director's office to sign forms.

topics.title: Year-end expense and budget report
topics.summary: The library director reported on the close of the fiscal year expense report. The library returned a little over $1,000 in unspent funds to the town across salaries and supply line items.
key_details: Returned just over $1,000 to the town general fund.
Hoopla digital media spending came in just under $900 out of a set-aside $1,000 budget.
Educational supplies balance ended near $100.

topics.title: Payable batch signature authorization
topics.summary: The board updated its authorization form with the town accounting department to permit all current library trustees to review and sign payable batches. This formal step allows newly appointed trustees to participate in reviewing invoices and signing payables.
key_details: Updates authorized signatures on file with town accounting.
Ensures new trustees can sign off on bills and learn library finances.

topics.title: Staff training on dementia and library closure request
topics.summary: Youth Services Librarian Mariana Sorensen requested permission to schedule a 90-minute training through Dementia Friends Massachusetts. The training would teach staff how to better interact with and support patrons experiencing dementia and their caregivers. The board supported holding the session during an early fall Monday afternoon, which will require closing the building for two hours, and suggested inviting staff from other town departments.
key_details: Presented by Youth Services Librarian Mariana Sorensen.
Session lasts 90 minutes and is offered free of charge.
Library will close for approximately two hours on a Monday afternoon, likely in September or October.
Trustees suggested inviting public safety, senior center, and Board of Health staff.
topics.outcome: Board voiced consensus support; scheduling to be finalized later.

topics.title: Facilities, lighting upgrades, and concrete repairs
topics.summary: The director provided an update on building maintenance handled in coordination with Facilities Director John Parent. Projects include replacing aging 1980s lighting fixtures with energy-efficient LED fixtures and addressing concrete surface degradation and cracking near the front entrance.
key_details: Consultants inspected library lighting fixtures to plan an LED replacement project.
Current bulbs fail frequently and fixtures date back to 1980s additions.
Staff are working with concrete contractors to smooth eroded walkways before the October book sale.
Director noted public Wi-Fi hotspots were in heavy demand during recent local internet outages.

topics.title: Staff promotions to library associate
topics.summary: Following a staff resignation that created vacant hours, the director recommended promoting two internal staff members into part-time library associate positions. The board approved promoting Anastasiia Kolvanaskova and Jackson Harris, both placed at Grade 2, Step 8 of Schedule A under the Salary Administration Plan.
key_details: Anastasiia Kolvanaskova promoted from part-time library technician to part-time library associate.
Jackson Harris promoted from part-time library page to part-time library associate.
Both positions compensated at Grade 2, Step 8 of Schedule A.
Fills staffing gaps created by a recent employee departure.

topics.title: Community Preservation Committee grant signage dispute
topics.summary: The board discussed wording for plaques required to close out older Community Preservation Act grants, including the front facade restoration. The trustees reaffirmed their preference that the signage thank the 'residents' of Southborough rather than 'citizens' or 'taxpayers.' A trustee volunteered to represent the board's position at an upcoming Community Preservation Committee meeting.
key_details: Signs are required to formally close out past CPA grants for archival work and facade restoration.
Library trustees unanimously favor the word 'residents' rather than 'citizens' or 'taxpayers.'
Trustee Janet Maney will represent the board at the next CPC meeting, with David Ekberg as alternate.
Existing CPA sign near the Little Free Library already uses 'residents.'
topics.outcome: Board agreed to advocate for its preferred wording at the next CPC meeting.

topics.title: DPW maintenance and landscaping coordination
topics.summary: Trustee Janet Maney reported on a discussion with Select Board member Kathy Cook regarding library landscaping, ongoing maintenance responsibilities, and long-term parking lot repairs. Town officials are reviewing the municipal landscaping contract and preparing an engineering scope to evaluate the library parking lot for future capital funding.
key_details: Landscaping contract is being reviewed by the town, with revisions to be shared with trustees.
Clarified that rain garden maintenance belongs to the town park, not library property.
Town will seek an engineering assessment for eventual parking lot repaving as a capital request.
Ongoing division of maintenance responsibilities between DPW and Facilities remains unresolved.

topics.title: IT infrastructure rewiring proposal
topics.summary: The director discussed an upcoming need to overhaul and rewire the library's internal IT network cabling after meeting with Town IT Director Jason Montio. Early estimates place the project cost around $30,000, and officials are considering whether to submit it as a town capital request or seek alternative funding.
key_details: Meeting held with IT Director Jason Montio regarding library network cabling deficiencies.
Rough preliminary cost estimated at approximately $30,000.
Project had originally been included in a state construction grant application that was not funded.
Board will weigh submitting a formal capital request versus using alternative reserves.
topics.outcome: Information presented; formal proposal expected at a future meeting.

votes.motion: Authorize all current members of the Board of Library Trustees to sign payable batches for the town accounting department.

Approve the library director's recommendation to promote Anastasiia Kolvanaskova from part-time library technician to part-time library associate at Grade 2, Step 8 of Schedule A of the Salary Administration Plan.
Approve the library director's recommendation to promote Jackson Harris from part-time library page to part-time library associate at Grade 2, Step 8 of Schedule A of the Salary Administration Plan.

public_comment.summary: Newly promoted employee Jackson Harris thanked the trustees for approving his promotion and shared that he recently graduated from college and plans to prepare for law school.

upcoming.what: Next regular Board of Library Trustees meeting
Community Preservation Committee meeting regarding grant signage wording
Two-hour library closure for staff Dementia Friends training
